name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog: Fixes a second, unrelated cause of federated playback failing with FFmpeg exit code 183 (0.0.81 fixed the token-starvation cause; this one hits even with a warm token cache). Root cause: an older version of MaterializeItem forced item.Container = "mp4" for every item on a WAN-capped Direct-mode server, regardless of the file's actual container - harmless while that capped URL was internal-only, but since reconciliation only ever creates and deletes items (never updates them in place), every item persisted under that version kept the wrong container forever. Jellyfin's transcoder demuxes the input using the item's stored container, so a real Matroska file with Container="mp4" made ffmpeg fail to parse it almost instantly - the client retried, and the cycle repeated forever. Confirmed live via a direct SQLite check of a stuck item's persisted Container. A one-time migration rebuilds every streamable federated item so it picks up its real container. Also: removed a dead MediaSources field from the federation sync fetch that did nothing but add one more collection Jellyfin's EF Core layer had to include on every synced page; fixed a client-side crash (document.createElement's old 2-arg form vs. jellyfin-web's webcomponents polyfill) that was silently killing Download/Hide and the download-progress rings on every federated item's detail page; and moved Download/Hide out of the detail page's button row into the native "..." more-commands menu, alongside Refresh metadata/Edit images/etc. 223 tests.
